summary: No truth or sourcing problems found. Every number was recomputed independently and agrees: radian ratios 0.9983342, 0.9999833, 0.9999998 (limit 1); degree ratios 0.01745241, 0.01745328, 0.01745329 (limit pi/180 = 0.01745329); sin 1 degree hand working (r^3/6 = 0.0000008861, sin 1 degree = 0.0174524064); forward difference at pi/3 with h = 0.01 gives 0.4956616 (sin(pi/3+0.01) = 0.8709820, cos 0.01 = 0.9999500004, (cos h - 1)/h = -0.0049999583), gap -0.00434 with correct negative sign explained as one-sided truncation error -(h/2) sin(pi/3) = -0.0043301; h = 0.001 gives 0.499567; central difference 0.4999917, gap -0.0000083, about 520 times smaller; pi/360 = 0.00873; cos 1 = 0.5403. The squeeze argument (1/2 sin t <= 1/2 t <= 1/2 tan t, hence cos t <= sin t / t <= 1, evenness for negative t) is valid, correctly locates radians in the sector-area line (t/2 versus pi t/360 in degrees), and the degree variant cos t° <= sin t° / (pi t/180) <= 1 is derived correctly. The L'Hopital and Maclaurin circularity objection is correct and is not presented as an HL prohibition. d/dx sin(x°) = (pi/180) cos(x°) is derived by the chain rule and linked to the horizontal stretch. Historical claims (Cotes 1714, Euler Introductio 1748, James Thomson at Queen's College Belfast 1873, Thomas Muir 1869/1874 and his 1910 letter) match the standard account, are explicitly flagged as recalled and unverified, name their sources (Cajori vol. 2, MacTutor) without inventing page numbers or journal issues, and the single Sources line tags every item '(recalled, not consulted)'; no supplied text existed. The IB formula-booklet claim is hedged with an instruction to check the student's own copy. Deterministic gate passed with zero Z3 errors. No marks were awarded, so no provisional label was required.
